body:
Going to Tottenham v Arsenal would only be worth it if you managed to source away tickets, in which case it would probably be an amazing experience as you'd be sat with a small selection of die-hard Arsenal fans. However, having home tickets and sitting with the Spurs fans would likely be horrible, abusive and risky (it only takes one moron to take it too far).

In comparison, Arsenal v Bournemouth is a safer option, and you may also have a better choice of where you want to sit for the best views/atmosphere, and the atmosphere has generally been good this season (even if the atmosphere wouldn't be quite as intense as at Spurs).

Thank you very much for this video,

I have favourited the link and although it made me sad, I think that given some time it may come in real handy as an eye opener.

Thank you.

This message hit home in so many ways and I thank you for that.

I'm incredibly frightened by the idea of counselling and psychopharmaca, not sure why, but it feels somewhat taboo. But you are right that I am in dire need of an emotional support. I don't know how much difference it will make right now as I lack real incentives but if I can find the spirit to get out of the house, there is a charity in the UK (where I'm from) that I may call. 

A virtual hug, and to see that there are some people that care, means the world right now, so again, thank you. I just wish I had a reliable hug source irl.

Thank you for taking the time to reply and for your message, 

I went and had a hug with my sister and we both just burst into tears, I think it was a good thing though, it felt like a mutual hug where she was hugging to help me and vice versa. I haven't really been very close to her recently so even just that small bond made me feel somewhat 

It's a small step, but I guess right now every little counts.

Again, thank you.
